intro: The docstrings leave some behaviour open. Each choice below follows the spec literally where it is clear, adds rather than removes, and adds no restriction the spec does not state.

decisions.decision: Responses contain every key the docstring shows, plus `id` and other useful fields; nothing is renamed or dropped.
decisions.why: Callers can rely on the documented shape and still refer back to records.

decisions.decision: Methods whose `:return:` is blank return `{}`.
decisions.why: The spec says output is JSON, so there is always valid JSON to parse.

decisions.decision: IDs are random UUID strings. An id that matches no record, including a malformed one, raises `NotFoundError`.
decisions.why: Opaque, unguessable ids; a malformed id can never match.

decisions.decision: Times are ISO 8601 in UTC, e.g. `2026-11-12T14:05:09Z`.
decisions.why: Unambiguous and sortable in any time zone.

decisions.decision: Lists are oldest first (team members: in the order they were added); ties are broken by name.
decisions.why: A stable, predictable order.

decisions.decision: Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; names and titles must not be empty; descriptions are optional and may be empty. Wrong types, `null` and non-object JSON are rejected.
decisions.why: Matches Django form behaviour and stops `"alice "` becoming a second Alice.

decisions.decision: Uniqueness is exact and case-sensitive.
decisions.why: The spec gives no other rule.

decisions.decision: Updates are partial: only the fields sent change, and at least one field must be sent.
decisions.why: A typo such as `display_nme` is reported instead of silently changing nothing.

decisions.decision: Unknown request keys are ignored.
decisions.why: Same treatment as `creation_time`; clients may send extra data.

decisions.decision: Display name: at most 64 characters on create, 128 on update.
decisions.why: Each docstring states its own limit.

evidence.code: * display name can be max 64 characters
evidence.quote: * display name can be max 64 characters

evidence.code: * display name can be max 128 characters
evidence.quote: * display name can be max 128 characters

decisions.decision: `update_user` accepts `name` only if it is unchanged.
decisions.why: The request format includes `name`, but "user name cannot be updated".

decisions.decision: `describe_user` returns `description` (the display name, since users have no description) and also `display_name`.
decisions.why: Keeps the documented key and adds the real field.

decisions.decision: `get_user_teams` lists the teams the user is a member of.
decisions.why: Membership is what links users to teams; see the admin rule below.

decisions.decision: The admin must be an existing user. Being admin does not make them a member or use one of the 50 places.
decisions.why: The spec keeps the admin field and membership separate; linking them would be a new rule.

decisions.decision: A team has at most 50 members, and an add or remove request lists at most 50 ids (an empty list is rejected).
decisions.why: A per-request cap alone would let a team grow without limit.

evidence.code: * Cap the max users that can be added to 50
evidence.quote: * Cap the max users that can be added to 50

decisions.decision: Adding an existing member or removing a non-member is skipped. An unknown user id fails the whole request.
decisions.why: Repeating a membership change is harmless; an unknown id is a real mistake.

decisions.decision: The same id sent twice counts once.
decisions.why: It names the same user.

decisions.decision: `add_task` needs a `board_id`.
decisions.why: The docstring has no board field, but a task cannot exist without a board.

evidence.code: :param request: A json string with the task details. Task is assigned to a user_id who works on the task
evidence.quote: :param request: A json string with the task details. Task is assigned to a user_id who works on the task

decisions.decision: In `add_task`, `title` is the task title and `user_id` is the assignee.
decisions.why: The docstring's placeholders (`<board_name>`, `<team id>`) contradict its own text: "assigned to a user_id who works on the task".

decisions.decision: A `creation_time` sent in `create_board` or `add_task` is ignored; the server records the time.
decisions.why: Timestamps stay trustworthy and cannot be backdated.

decisions.decision: The assignee can be any existing user, not only a team member.
decisions.why: The spec does not require membership.

decisions.decision: A task can move between OPEN, IN_PROGRESS and COMPLETE in any direction while its board is open. Tasks on a closed board are frozen.
decisions.why: No workflow is specified. Reopening a task would break the rule that closed boards are all COMPLETE.

decisions.decision: A board with no tasks can be closed. Closing an already closed board is an error and keeps the original `end_time`.
decisions.why: No tasks means none are incomplete; the first end time is the real one.

evidence.code: * You can only close boards with all tasks marked as COMPLETE
evidence.quote: * You can only close boards with all tasks marked as COMPLETE

decisions.decision: `list_boards` returns open boards only.
decisions.why: The method is documented as "list all open boards for a team".

evidence.code: # list all open boards for a team
evidence.quote: # list all open boards for a team

decisions.decision: A board name stays taken after the board is closed.
decisions.why: "Unique for a team" covers all of the team's boards.

decisions.decision: Exports never overwrite: the file is `<team>_<board>_<UTC time>.txt`, with `-2`, `-3`… on a clash. `out_file` is the file name inside `out/`. Closed boards can be exported.
decisions.why: Every export is kept, and file names are safe on any system.
